images.caption: Two w:Lustron houses on Nicollet Avenue between 50th and 51st Streets in Minneapolis, Minnesota.

place.source_title: Lustron houses, Nicollet Avenue between 50th and 51st Streets

brief: One of a pair of Lustron prefabricated enamelled-steel houses (c.1949): a one-storey gabled box with square pale-blue steel wall panels, a steel-tile roof, a recessed corner entrance porch, a big picture window, a boxed bay and aluminum awning; its yellow twin next door and a Tudor Revival house behind, in winter snow.

facade.notes: a row of Lustrons on Nicollet Avenue (Minneapolis, 1949), each enamel colour different (yellow, blue, grey), aluminium awnings, set up a slope with concrete steps and pipe rails from the sidewalk; spruces; an older Tudor house behind; deep snow

why.note: factory-built steel houses: a 1949 row bought together
Lustron's four enamel colours (blue, yellow, grey, tan) made identical houses read as different
